events.title: Assassination of Julius Caesar
events.description: Roman dictator Julius Caesar was stabbed to death by a group of senators led by Marcus Junius Brutus and Gaius Cassius Longinus during a meeting of the Senate on the Ides of March.
events.significance: Caesar's assassination triggered a series of civil wars that destroyed the Roman Republic and led to the rise of Augustus and the Roman Empire.

events.title: Columbus Returns from His First Voyage
events.description: Christopher Columbus arrived back in Palos de la Frontera, Spain, after his first voyage across the Atlantic, bringing news of lands in the Americas to the Spanish crown.
events.significance: His return opened the era of sustained European contact with the Americas, with profound consequences for global trade, colonization, and the peoples of both hemispheres.

events.title: Maine Admitted as the 23rd U.S. State
events.description: Maine became the 23rd state of the United States as part of the Missouri Compromise, separating from Massachusetts and entering the Union as a free state.
events.significance: The admission balanced the entry of slave-holding Missouri and temporarily preserved the sectional balance between free and slave states in the U.S. Senate.

events.title: Abdication of Tsar Nicholas II
events.description: Amid the February Revolution, Tsar Nicholas II abdicated the Russian throne (March 15 by the Gregorian calendar), ending more than three centuries of Romanov rule.
events.significance: The abdication ended the Russian monarchy, led to the Provisional Government, and set the stage for the Bolshevik Revolution and the creation of the Soviet Union.

events.title: German Occupation of Czechoslovakia
events.description: Nazi Germany invaded and occupied the remaining Czech lands of Czechoslovakia, establishing the Protectorate of Bohemia and Moravia in violation of the Munich Agreement.
events.significance: The occupation demonstrated the failure of appeasement and prompted Britain and France to abandon that policy, hastening the outbreak of World War II.
